subject.title: Feature request: fallback model chain for compaction and LCM summaryModel

question: Should OpenClaw add a core `agents.defaults.compaction.fallbacks` config field now, and should any Lossless summary fallback remain plugin-owned through `fallbackProviders` or become a generic context-engine SDK contract?
rationale: This is not a narrow bug fix: it adds provider/auth routing behavior, a new config/default surface, and crosses the core compaction plus external Lossless context-engine boundary.

options.title: Approve Core Compaction Fallbacks Only
options.body: Add an explicit core `agents.defaults.compaction.fallbacks` contract while documenting Lossless `fallbackProviders` as the plugin-owned LCM answer unless a missing SDK seam appears.

options.title: Design A Unified Context-Engine Fallback Contract
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers choose one API for embedded compaction and plugin-owned context-engine summarizers.

options.title: Decline New Core Config
options.body: Keep exact `compaction.model` behavior and ask operators to use session model fallbacks, compaction providers, or plugin-owned fallback routing.

recommendation.title: Approve Core Compaction Fallbacks Only
recommendation.body: Add an explicit core `agents.defaults.compaction.fallbacks` contract while documenting Lossless `fallbackProviders` as the plugin-owned LCM answer unless a missing SDK seam appears.

likelyOwner.reason: The open choice centers on context-engine/plugin ownership and compaction config semantics, and jalehman is tied to both the original compaction model merge and context-engine delegate history.
